Leo (acme-inc): hitting 403 on /v1/generate after rotating keys, curl gives 403 {"error":"forbidden","reason":"org_mismatch"}, request_id=req_12ab34cd. Anyone seen this?

Maya (support): hi Leo — can you paste the exact curl you used and the request id? also your org id if ok to share.

Leo (acme-inc): sure, here's curl (sanitized):
```bash
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-prod_123" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"redwood-7b", "input":"hi"}'
```
Response: 403 + body: {"error":"forbidden","reason":"org_mismatch"} request_id=req_12ab34cd org_id: org_456

Maya (support): thanks. Two things to check: a) token scope/ownership — is sk-prod_123 minted under org_789? b) do you pass X-Redwood-Org header? Usually org-scoped tokens require org header if not default. Can you try with header `X-Redwood-Org: org_456` and add `-v` to curl to include headers?

Leo (acme-inc): tried adding header, still 403. here's verbose output (sanitized):
```text
> POST /v1/generate HTTP/1.1
> Host: api.redwood.ai
> Authorization: Bearer sk-prod_123
> X-Redwood-Org: org_456
< HTTP/1.1 403 Forbidden
< Content-Type: application/json
< x-redwood-request-id: req_12ab34cd
{"error":"forbidden","reason":"org_mismatch"}
```
Also attached the request id.

Sam (eng-api): I pulled logs for req_12ab34cd — from server side we see token metadata owner_org=org_789, token_scopes=[generate], incoming org header=org_456. Server checks owner_org==incoming_org -> mismatch -> 403. Log snippet:
```text
2025-06-12T14:23:11.345Z INFO req=req_12ab34cd auth: token_owner=org_789 token_id=sk-prod_123 incoming_org=org_456 result=org_mismatch
```
Looks like token was created under the wrong org.

Priya (sre): another common gotcha — if customer created token in the 'Personal' area, tokens are personal and tied to a user org, not the account org. Also double-check project vs org header — if you've been using 'X-Project' in other products it won't work.

Maya (support): action items: Leo — can you confirm whether you intended token to be for org_456 or org_789? If you need to repro we can issue a temporary token to test in your session. Also please run the full debug bundle: curl with `--trace-ascii debug.txt` and paste the first 50 lines; include exact request_id.

Leo (acme-inc): Confirmed token was minted in a different org by mistake (partner onboarding). Can you issue a temp token please. Also how do I rotate cleanly w/out downtime?

Maya (support): We'll issue temp token scoped to org_456 and share via secure channel. For rotation: create new key under org_456, update clients to use new key, then revoke old after TTL. For immediate repro I generated temp token: sk-temp_xyZ (expires in 30m) — try:
```bash
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \
 -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-temp_xyZ" \
 -H "X-Redwood-Org: org_456" \
 -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
 -d '{"model":"redwood-7b","input":"test"}'
```

Leo (acme-inc): Using temp token — success 200, request id=req_12ab34ef. Thanks Maya. Will rotate keys and update apps.

Maya (support): great — I'll attach server log lines showing success for record:
```text
2025-06-12T14:31:05.102Z INFO req=req_12ab34ef auth: token_owner=org_456 token_id=sk-temp_xyZ incoming_org=org_456 result=ok
```
Closing this thread; reopen if anything else.
